title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues to Be Noted by the People's Courts in Hearing Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases at Present
keywords_en: bankruptcy; people's court hearing enterprise bankruptcy cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Certain Issues to Be Noted by People's Courts in Currently Handling Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases

Fa Fa [1997] No. 2

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

In recent years, the number of enterprise bankruptcy cases accepted by the People's Courts has increased year by year. Particularly since the State Council launched pilot work in certain cities to optimize the capital structure of enterprises and establish and improve a mechanism for survival of the fittest, the number of enterprise bankruptcy cases has risen considerably. In order to correctly and promptly handle such cases, notice is hereby given on certain issues to be noted by the People's Courts in currently handling enterprise bankruptcy cases as follows:

1. When handling enterprise bankruptcy cases, the People's Courts must be both proactive and very cautious. This shall be conducive to promoting the adjustment of industrial structure and establishing a modern enterprise system; it shall prevent circumvention of the law and evasion of debt, thereby avoiding the loss of state-owned assets; it shall discard narrow-minded local protectionism, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of creditors and debtors in accordance with the law; and it shall maintain social stability, so as to serve the establishment and improvement of the socialist market economic system.

2. When accepting an enterprise bankruptcy case, the People's Court shall carefully examine whether the bankruptcy application filed by the party concerned satisfies the conditions stipulated in the Bankruptcy Law of the PRC (For Trial Implementation) (hereinafter referred to as the "Enterprise Bankruptcy Law"), the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Procedure Law"), and other relevant laws, regulations, and policies, and shall strictly handle the case filing stage. For those cases that do not meet the acceptance conditions, acceptance shall be denied in accordance with the law. Cases of sham bankruptcy and genuine debt evasion shall be strictly prevented.

3. The provisions on bankruptcy in the "Notice of the State Council on Issues Concerning the Implementation of Bankruptcy of State-owned Enterprises in Certain Cities" (Guo Fa [1994] No. 59) (hereinafter referred to as the "Notice"), the "Supplementary Notice of the State Council on Issues Concerning the Implementation of Merger and Bankruptcy of State-owned Enterprises and the Reemployment of Workers in Certain Cities" (Guo Fa [1997] No. 10) (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplementary Notice"), and the "Notice on Certain Issues Concerning the Trial Implementation of Merger and Bankruptcy of State-owned Enterprises" (Guo Jing Mao Qi [1996] No. 492) approved by the State Council and issued by the State Economic and Trade Commission and the People's Bank of China shall apply only to state-owned industrial enterprises within the pilot cities designated by the State Council for "Optimizing Enterprise Capital Structure" (hereinafter referred to as "pilot cities"). These provisions shall not apply under any circumstances to bankruptcy cases of enterprises in non-pilot cities or to bankruptcy cases of non-state-owned industrial enterprises in pilot cities. For bankruptcy cases that were already accepted by the People's Courts in pilot cities in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Notice prior to the issuance of the Supplementary Notice, the provisions of the Notice shall continue to apply. Bankruptcy applications shall not be accepted temporarily for state-owned industrial enterprises whose repayment obligations for loans or on-lent funds borrowed from foreign governments have not yet been fulfilled.

4. When handling an enterprise bankruptcy case, the People's Court shall conduct a thorough liquidation of the property of the bankrupt enterprise. The members of the liquidation group shall be representative and shall be designated by the People's Court from among the department in charge of the bankrupt enterprise, the local Economic and Trade Commission (Planning and Economic Commission, Economic Commission), the Department (Bureau) of Finance, the Land Administration Bureau, the State-owned Assets Administration Department, the People's Bank of China or its branches (sub-branches), and other relevant departments and professionals. The head of the liquidation group shall be designated by the People's Court. The liquidation group is responsible to the People's Court and shall report on its work.

The main duties of the liquidation group are: to protect the bankrupt property, to liquidate claims and debts, to prepare a detailed property schedule and balance sheet, to prepare a distribution plan, to handle and distribute the bankrupt property in accordance with the law, to lawfully conduct necessary civil activities, to submit a liquidation report, to handle matters concerning the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings such as the cancellation of enterprise registration, and to complete other matters lawfully designated by the People's Court.

5. The creditors' meeting shall be composed of all creditors who have lawfully filed claims. The head office or branch (sub-branch) of the bank that is a creditor of the bankrupt enterprise shall send a representative to participate in the creditors' meeting. The chairperson of the creditors' meeting shall be designated by the People's Court from among the creditors who have voting rights. The main duties of the creditors' meeting are: to examine the evidentiary materials concerning claims, to confirm whether claims are secured by property and the amount thereof; to discuss and pass the draft composition agreement; to review the liquidation, audit, and appraisal reports of the liquidation group; and to discuss and pass the plan for the disposal and distribution of the bankrupt property.

All members of the creditors' meeting have voting rights, except for creditors with secured property who have not waived their right to preferential satisfaction. Resolutions of the meeting are binding on all creditors. If the liquidation group proposes a plan for the distribution of the bankrupt property, and after repeated consultations it is difficult for the creditors' meeting to pass the plan, the People's Court shall make a ruling in accordance with the law.

6. When handling enterprise bankruptcy cases, the People's Courts shall take care to prevent debtors from using bankruptcy to evade debts. Acts such as concealing, distributing privately, or transferring property without compensation, selling property at a reduced price, making early repayment of debts not yet due, and waiving claims, committed by the bankrupt enterprise for the purpose of evading debts, shall be lawfully confirmed as invalid, and the property shall be recovered. Claims held by the bankrupt enterprise against others shall be lawfully recovered and included in the bankrupt property.

7. Where the handling of an enterprise bankruptcy case by the People's Court involves issues concerning the legal validity of mortgage contracts and secured claims, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the Guarantee Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Guarantee Law"), the Notice, the Supplementary Notice, and this notice, carefully examine and correctly determine the validity of the mortgage contract. In any of the following circumstances, the mortgage contract shall be determined to be invalid: where a state-owned enterprise mortgages key equipment, complete sets of equipment, or important buildings as determined, without the approval of the competent government department; where property that may not be used as collateral as stipulated in Article 37 of the Guarantee Law is used to create a mortgage; where the bankrupt enterprise creates a mortgage on a debt that was originally unsecured during the period from six months prior to the People's Court's acceptance of the enterprise bankruptcy case up to the declaration of bankruptcy; or where, in the presence of multiple creditors, the debtor and an individual creditor maliciously collude to mortgage the majority of the debtor's property to a single creditor, thereby rendering the debtor unable to perform its other debts.

8. Before disposing of the property of a bankrupt enterprise, the People's Court shall arrange for a property appraisal institution recognized by the competent department for the administration of state-owned assets of the State Council to conduct a property appraisal. The property appraisal must be realistic and truthful; undervaluation for the purpose of low appraisal or overvaluation is strictly prohibited. When disposing of the property of a bankrupt enterprise, methods such as auction shall be adopted as far as possible to prevent low-price transfers and to avoid loss of state-owned assets or damage to the legitimate interests of creditors; debts shall not be offset by delivery of property in kind without approval by the creditors' meeting or a ruling by the People's Court.

9. When handling bankruptcy cases of state-owned industrial enterprises in pilot cities, the People's Courts shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Notice and the Supplementary Notice, transfer the right to use land mainly by means of auction or bidding. The proceeds from such transfer shall first be used to settle the workers of the bankrupt enterprise. The expenses for settling workers shall be strictly determined in accordance with the provisions of the Notice and the Supplementary Notice, and the standards shall not be arbitrarily raised or the scope expanded.

10. When handling bankruptcy cases, the People's Courts shall endeavor to reduce the costs of bankruptcy. Depending on the specific circumstances of the case, court fees may be appropriately reduced or waived. The scope of and principles governing the payment of bankruptcy expenses shall be examined and approved by the creditors' meeting. Fees for appraisals, audits, and the like shall be carefully examined and paid at the minimum amount necessary to ensure the work requirements.

11. Higher People's Courts shall effectively strengthen their guidance and supervision over the handling of enterprise bankruptcy cases by lower People's Courts. If a higher People's Court finds that a ruling made by a lower People's Court is indeed erroneous, it shall notify the lower court to correct the error in accordance with the law. Where necessary, the higher court may issue a ruling directing the lower People's Court to make a new ruling.

12. The provisions of this notice concerning the handling of bankruptcy cases of state-owned industrial enterprises in pilot cities shall also apply to bankruptcy cases of state-owned industrial enterprises in pilot cities that may be designated by the State Council in the future.

March 6, 1997
